summary.body: Comment-only change, no behavior change as claimed. The new comment correctly explains the `n > len(items)` case, but it stops short of the edge case that actually surprises callers: `n == 0` (and negative `n`) don't behave like "the last n items" at all, since `items[-0:]` is `items[0:]`, i.e. the *whole* list, not an empty one. Worth a one-line addendum to the comment (or a guard in the code) so the documented behavior matches what a reader would expect from the function's name.

items.markdown: The added comment documents the `n > len(items)` case but omits the more surprising edge case: for `n == 0`, `items[-n:]` becomes `items[0:]`, returning the *entire* list rather than an empty one (and negative `n` drops from the front instead of taking from the back). Given the whole point of this change is to document `last_n`'s edge-case behavior, this gap seems worth closing — either extend the comment to call out `n <= 0`, or add an explicit guard (e.g. `if n <= 0: return []`) if that behavior was never intended.
